QF.id: AIFM CIII Fund Monitoring Reporting and Exit_3

question.text: Satpura Market-Neutral Fund (close-ended, 5-year tenure) has 20 investors with total invested value of INR 300 crore. The Manager seeks approval to extend tenure by 2 years. Investors with INR 195 crore (by value of their investment) vote YES, INR 75 crore vote NO, INR 30 crore abstain. Is the two-thirds-by-value-of-investment approval obtained?

answer.text: No — abstentions are counted as NO, giving 195/300 = 65%

explanation.text: The Logic: Tenure extension of a close-ended Cat III AIF requires approval from at least two-thirds of unit holders by value of their investment in the scheme. 195 / 300 = 65.00%, which falls short of 66.67%. The resolution fails. Abstentions function as non-consent because they are not counted towards the YES tally on the total invested value base. The Trap: Option A rounds two-thirds to 65% — wrong. Option C uses 'votes cast' as the denominator, but the AIF rule uses the total value of investment. Option D correctly fails but with wrong reasoning (abstentions are not 'counted as NO' — they simply are not counted as YES, which has the same arithmetic effect here). Note: The two-thirds-by-value-of-investment threshold is the standard rule for tenure extension of a close-ended Cat III AIF scheme (per workbook pp. 398-399). Higher thresholds (such as 75% by value) apply to different decisions like entry into the Dissolution Period.
